title: length, length(), size()
prompt: Which is correct for an `int[] a`?
explanation: Arrays: `.length` (field). Strings: `.length()` (method). Collections: `.size()`. Mixing these up is a rite of passage — get it over with now.

title: Largest element
prompt: Return the largest value in `nums` (always non-empty). Track a running max starting at `nums[0]`.

tests.note: all negative — don't start max at 0!

solution.explanation: Seeding with `nums[0]` (or `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, not 0) handles all-negative arrays — a classic hidden-test trap. One pass: O(n).

hints: Keep a 'best so far' variable and update it as you walk the array.
Start `max` at `nums[0]`, not 0 — think about an all-negative array.
`max = Math.max(max, x)` inside the loop.

title: Reference semantics
prompt: After `int[] a = {1, 2}; int[] b = a; b[0] = 9;` — what is `a[0]`?
options: `9` — a and b point at the same array
explanation: Assignment copies the reference, not the data. For an independent copy: `int[] b = Arrays.copyOf(a, a.length);`

title: Predict the output: comparing arrays
prompt: Predict exactly what each line prints.
explanation: `a` and `b` are two separate array objects, so `==` (same reference?) is false even with equal contents. `c = a` copies the reference, so `a == c` is true. `Arrays.equals` compares element by element → true. `Arrays.toString` formats as `[1, 2, 3]`.

title: Sorting an int[] descending
prompt: You have an `int[] nums` and need it in descending order. What works?
options: `Arrays.sort(nums);` then reverse it with a two-pointer swap
explanation: For primitive arrays `Arrays.sort` only sorts ascending. The comparator overload `Arrays.sort(arr, comparator)` only accepts object arrays like `Integer[]` — passing an `int[]` doesn't compile. The other two methods don't exist. Sort ascending, then reverse in O(n).

title: Same elements, any order
prompt: Return whether `a` and `b` contain exactly the same values with the same counts, in any order. Sort both, then compare with `Arrays.equals`. (Modifying the inputs is fine.)

solution.explanation: Sorting puts equal multisets into identical order, and `Arrays.equals` checks length plus every position. `a == b` would compare references and always be false here. O(n log n) for the sorts.

hints: If two arrays hold the same values, what do they look like once both are put in order?
`Arrays.sort` both arrays first.
Compare contents with `Arrays.equals(a, b)` — not `==`.

title: Count in a grid
prompt: Return how many cells in `grid` equal `target`. Nested loops over rows and columns.

solution.explanation: `grid.length` is the row count; `grid[0].length` is the column count. Every cell is visited once: O(rows x cols).

hints: Visit every cell once and keep a counter.
Outer loop `r` over `grid.length`, inner loop `c` over `grid[0].length`.

title: Recall: the dirs loop
prompt: Complete the 4-direction neighbor loop with its bounds check.
explanation: Each direction is `{rowDelta, colDelta}`, so `d[0]` moves the row and `d[1]` the column. Rows are bounded by `grid.length`, columns by `grid[0].length`, and `continue` skips neighbors that fall off the grid.

title: Drill: count land neighbors
prompt: From memory: return how many of the 4 neighbors (up, down, left, right) of cell `(r, c)` are inside the grid and equal `1`. Use the `dirs` table and a single bounds check.

tests.note: corner: two neighbors are off the grid

solution.explanation: The direction table turns four near-identical blocks into one loop. The bounds check runs before any read, and `||` short-circuits, so an off-grid index is never used. O(1) per cell — this is the inner step of every grid BFS/DFS.

hints: Describe the four moves as data (row change, column change) and loop over them.
Skip the neighbor if `nr` or `nc` is outside `[0, grid.length)` / `[0, grid[0].length)`; otherwise count it when it's 1.

title: Drill: array sum
prompt: From memory: return the sum of all elements using an enhanced for loop (`for (int x : nums)`).

solution.explanation: Accumulator declared before the loop, updated inside, returned after. An empty array skips the loop and returns 0. O(n).

hints: You need a running total that exists before the loop starts.
Enhanced for: `for (int x : nums)` — add each `x` to the total.

title: Drill: reverse in place
prompt: From memory: reverse `nums` in place using the two-pointer swap — `l` from the front, `r` from the back, swap and move inward while `l < r`. The method returns nothing; the grader checks the mutated array.

solution.explanation: Each swap fixes both ends; stopping at `l < r` leaves an odd middle untouched. The three-line swap with a temp variable is pure muscle memory. O(n) time, O(1) space.

hints: Swap the outermost pair, then move both pointers one step inward.
Loop header: `for (int l = 0, r = nums.length - 1; l < r; l++, r--)`.
Swap needs a temp: `int t = nums[l]; nums[l] = nums[r]; nums[r] = t;`

title: Recall: create & fill
prompt: Fill in the array creation, fill, and length operations.
code:
int[] a = new int[{{1}}];     // n zero-filled slots
Arrays.{{2}}(a, -1);           // set every slot to -1
int len = a.{{3}};             // number of slots (no parentheses!)
explanation: `new int[n]` allocates n zeros, `Arrays.fill` overwrites them, and `.length` is a field (no parentheses).

title: Drill: build a filled array
prompt: From memory: return a new `int[]` of length `n` with every element equal to `val`.

solution.explanation: `new int[n]` allocates n zeros; `Arrays.fill` overwrites every slot. `n = 0` gives an empty array, which is valid. O(n).

hints: Two steps: allocate the right size, then set every slot.
Allocate with `new int[n]`; the `Arrays` toolbox has a one-call way to set every slot.

title: Recall: sort & copy
prompt: Fill in the sort and sub-range copy operations.
code:
Arrays.{{1}}(a);                       // ascending, in place
int[] sub = Arrays.{{2}}(a, 1, 4);     // copy indices [1, 4)
explanation: `Arrays.sort` sorts in place; `Arrays.copyOfRange(a, from, to)` copies the half-open range [from, to).

title: Drill: sort ascending
prompt: From memory: sort `nums` ascending in place and return it (one `Arrays.sort` call).

solution.explanation: `Arrays.sort` works in place and returns `void`, so sort first and then return the same array reference. O(n log n).

hints: The `Arrays` toolbox sorts in place — it doesn't hand back a new array.
Call the sort on `nums` as its own statement, then `return nums;`.
